content_preview.title: Jujutsu 0.46.0 Adds Colocated Workspaces Backed by Git Worktrees, New jj file edit and delete Commands and Multi-Remote Push
content_preview.summary: Jujutsu 0.46.0, released October 7, can create Git worktrees alongside extra workspaces, raises the minimum Git version to 2.42.0 and lists seven breaking changes.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Jujutsu (`jj`), the Git-compatible version control system, shipped version 0.46.0 on October 7, 2026, according to the [project changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jj-vcs/jj/v0.46.0/CHANGELOG.md). The [release notes on GitHub](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/releases/tag/v0.46.0) name a single highlight: "Jujutsu can now colocate workspaces besides the default one by creating Git worktrees." editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured Briefing (761 words by whitespace split, matching the script count; range 300-800). Sections: Overview, What Changed, Breaking Changes, Fixes, What We Don't Know, Related Coverage. Appropriate technical depth, no editorializing.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both gzipped snapshots. source-0.html.gz (GitHub release page v0.46.0, 200, ~230KB HTML) and source-1.html.gz (raw CHANGELOG.md at tag v0.46.0, 200, ~219KB text). Both hostnames (github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com) are already on config/source_allowlist.txt; no allowlist edit needed. suspicious_patterns is null for both. Snapshot sanity: the release page snapshot is full (release body, contributors, assets), not thin. Live re-check via GitHub API (repos/jj-vcs/jj/releases/tags/v0.46.0): published 2026-10-07T21:28:17Z, not draft/prerelease, tag v0.46.0 resolves (7d38231); the API release body is textually identical to the CHANGELOG 0.46.0 section (whitespace-normalized diff shows only an extra 'About' blurb on the release page). Every changelog bullet of the 0.46.0 section was matched against the release-page text with zero misses. The two sources are therefore NOT independent: the release notes are a copy of the changelog, both first-party from the jj-vcs project. For a Briefing that reports what a release says it contains this is acceptable, and the article attributes claims to 'the changelog' or 'release notes' and makes no independent claims (e.g. no performance claims). Claim-by-claim: (1) released 2026-10-07: changelog heading '[0.46.0] - 2026-10-07' and release page date, confirmed. (2) Highlight quote 'Jujutsu can now colocate workspaces besides the default one by creating Git worktrees.' verbatim; 'jj workspace add --[no-]colocate' and 'git.colocate' confirmed. (3) --colocate/--no-colocate, default colocates when current workspace colocated and git.colocate true, 'jj workspace forget' removes worktree: confirmed. (4) 'jj git colocation status/enable/disable' work on child workspaces; status reports state and workspace name; enable creates worktree, disable removes it: confirmed. (5) 'jj workspace remove' removes workspace and directory, working-copy state snapshotted into a commit: confirmed. (6) Quote 'Added commands jj file edit and jj file delete for editing files in any revision without needing to change the working copy.' verbatim (backticks dropped in rendering). (7) jj git push multiple remotes, git.push string pattern or array, repeatable --remote accepting patterns, revsets.git-push: confirmed. (8) Smaller additions ($path/$line with example ui.editor = ["emacs", "+$line", "$path"], aliases.<name>.enabled = false for built-in and later-layer aliases, jj util diff <path1> <path2>): confirmed. (9) Seven breaking changes verified individually, count is exactly seven and in changelog order: min git 2.42.0 up from 2.41.0 with git worktree add --orphan added in 2.42.0; MSRV 1.97.1; jj bisect run consistency checks and --trust-endpoints; jj split single editor session; jj undo/redo refuse cross-workspace operations unless --allow-cross-workspace; jj workspace list/root show all recorded paths with warnings in root; List.get()/first()/last() return Option<T>. All confirmed. The summary's 'seven breaking changes' is correct. (10) Fixes: Windows ssh prompt hang, Windows colocation enable/disable 'Access is denied (os error 5)' with pack files, undo of workspace forget preserves path, .gitignore respected under sparse patterns: confirmed. No contributor credits appear in the article, so none to verify. Related link /article/2026-06/26-jujutsu-042-switches-to-the-mimalloc-allocator-and-removes-a-batch-of-deprecated-commands uses the correct singular form and resolves to an existing published article whose title matches the description (0.42, mimalloc, deprecated commands removal). Orphan-link diff: every body URL is in article.sources and vice versa (internal link excluded); no gap.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All numbers, flag names, command names, versions and dates trace to the cited changelog/release notes. No hallucinated quotes. The 'What We Don't Know' statements (no benchmarks, no distro Git-floor timing) are accurate: neither source contains such data.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, descriptive, attributed throughout. No AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: New release (0.46.0). Only prior Jujutsu release coverage is the June 0.42 article; no overlap.
concerns: Both sources are the same first-party text (release notes mirror the changelog), so there is no independent corroboration; acceptable for a release-notes Briefing since every claim is attributed to the project's own notes.
Word count 761 is close to the 800 cap but within range.
recommendations: Where available, add an independent secondary source (e.g. Git project docs for 'git worktree add --orphan' in 2.42) for context in future release briefings.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: APPROVE. Accurate, fully attributed, all seven breaking changes and every command/flag/version verified against both snapshots and the live GitHub API; link integrity and schema checks pass.
